gameStory.articleHeadline: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons lead the Bears past the Seahawks 34-17
gameStory.articleDescription: — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention...
gameStory.articleStory: SEATTLE -- — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention with important games on big stages. Then he delivered exactly what the Bears needed. Simmons had a sack in his Bears debut as part of a dominant defensive performance that helped lead Chicago to a 34-17 victory over the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night. “When I attacked the field, I wasn’t worried about the trade,” Simmons said. “I wasn’t worried about all the outside noise. All I was worried about is play after play, just give the team everything I got.” Acquired last week from Tennessee for a package that included two first-round picks, Simmons took little time to make a big impact on a defense that had lacked difference-makers. He had a sack on the opening drive, added another tackle for loss and finished with six tackles, three pressures and a pass defensed with coach Ben Johnson describing his impact as “profound." Chicago held Seattle to 252 yards and one third-down conversion on 11 tries. “He has me up off of the bench,” receiver Rome Odunze said. “Watching them third downs, watching the defense in general to see what he’s going to do next. He brings the energy to them. whatToWatch.text: That defense is the real deal — 17.9 points allowed per game is the kind of number that wins January football, and they're doing it with Uchenna Nwosu and Brandon Pili among five guys ruled out. Lumen is going to be loud.

Pass rush vs. pass rush: Seattle's getting home 2.43 times a game, Chicago 2.71. Whichever front wrecks the pocket first probably decides this one, and a 46.5 total says oddsmakers expect somebody to get uncomfortable.

4-3 with a win streak on the line, laying just 3 at home — this is a prove-it spot, not a gimme. The Bears are shorthanded too (five out, including Case Keenum and Malik Muhammad II), so there are no excuses left on the table for either side.

recap.text: Monday night at Lumen Field turned ugly fast, as Chicago's revamped front — with newly acquired Jeffery Simmons notching a sack in his Bears debut — suffocated Seattle in a 34-17 loss. The Seahawks managed just one conversion on 11 third downs and never found rhythm, scraping together 252 yards while Caleb Williams picked them apart, including a 1-yard touchdown toss to Luther Burden III on the opening series. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 43-yard strike from Sam Darnold and a Cooper Kupp 7-yard score with a two-point conversion pulled Seattle within striking distance in the fourth, but D'Andre Swift answered with back-to-back 5-yard touchdown runs to bury the comeback. Each team coughed up one turnover, but only one offense ever looked comfortable.

newsBlurb.text: Lumen Field hosts the Bears on Monday night, and the Week 8 spotlight belongs entirely to Seattle. Chicago walks into the loudest building in the league with no Sunday crowd noise to hide behind — a standalone national window, one game, full volume.
